name: Spatial UI (visionOS)
summary: Translucent glass windows that float in the user's room at a set distance, lit by the surrounding scene and controlled by eye gaze and hand pinch. Apple introduced it with Vision Pro in 2023.

philosophy.core_thesis: An interface in space should be a physical presence in the room, so it uses glass that takes light from the real scene and respects the person's field of view.
design_principles: Make windows from a glass material that blends with the room behind it; a standard window is about 1280pt by 720pt at 2 metres distance.
Place content where the eyes rest, within a field of about 30 degrees, and avoid forcing head turns.
Make every target at least 60pt, with 16pt or more of spacing, because eye and pinch input is less precise than a mouse.
Show hover with a highlight on the gazed element, because the eyes are the cursor and the pinch is the click.
Use depth for meaning: lift a modal by 20pt to 40pt in front of its window with a soft shadow.
Use a corner radius of 24pt to 32pt on windows and a full capsule shape on buttons.
Set text in vibrant white or dark label colours that stay legible on glass, at 17pt or larger and weight 500 or more.
anti_patterns: Opaque dark backgrounds that block the room
Targets smaller than 44pt on an eye-and-pinch device
Text below 17pt or below weight 400 on glass
Hard black drop shadows and flat hard borders
Content pinned to the head at a close distance, which causes eye strain
Windows wider than the field of view, so that the edges need head turns
Fast parallax or large moves toward the viewer

layout.grid_mechanics: Windows are flat planes of 1280pt by 720pt or larger placed at 1 to 3 metres; inside, a 12-column grid with 16pt to 24pt gutters holds content, and ornaments sit on the window edge.
layout.whitespace_ratio: 40–55% of the window stays open; the spacing scale is 8, 12, 16, 24, 32 and 48pt, and the minimum target gap is 16pt.
layout.alignment_rules: Content aligns to a window's inner padding of 24pt; toolbars float as ornaments at the bottom edge, offset 20pt outside the window; windows stay at eye level and are never above 30 degrees up.
layout.container_geometry: Windows have a 32pt radius; cards a 24pt radius; buttons are capsules of 44pt to 60pt height; 3D objects sit inside volumes that keep a 1:1:1 or 4:3 bounding box.

font_pairings.note: An open stand-in for SF Pro at weights 500, 600 and 700.
Rounder display forms that match the capsule buttons.
One family at weights 500 and 700, with strong stems for glass.

typography.tracking: Display sizes take 0.00em to -0.01em; body takes +0.01em; small captions take +0.02em for legibility on glass.
hierarchy_rules: Set the body at 17pt, the title at 28pt and the large title at 48pt; do not go below 12pt anywhere.
Use weight 500 or 600 for body and 700 for titles, because thin text vanishes on glass.
Use white text with vibrancy on glass at 100%, 60% and 40% opacity for primary, secondary and tertiary labels.
Centre short titles and left-align paragraphs; keep lines to 45 to 60 characters.

color.palette_structure: A glass material in place of a background colour, white labels at three opacities, and one system tint for the primary action; the room supplies the rest of the colour.
color.contrast_rules: Glass takes colour from the room, so contrast cannot be set in advance; use white labels with vibrancy and keep to 4.5:1 for text over the worst-case dark and bright rooms, and add a 30% scrim where the system material cannot reach it.
color.surface_treatment: A system glass material of rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.15) with backdrop-filter blur(40px) saturate(180%); a specular edge gradient at the border adds the sense of a thick pane.
color.light_and_shadow: Windows take light from the real room and from a virtual light above; each window casts a soft shadow of 0 20px 60px rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.35) to the floor, and raised elements add a specular rim of 1px rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.4).

materiality.surface_simulation: Thick frosted glass that picks up the colour and light of the real room, with a specular rim and a soft shadow on the surfaces behind it.
materiality.border_rules: 1px specular rim of rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.4) on the top and left edges, fading to 0.1 on the bottom and right; no solid borders; focus uses a 2pt white ring.
materiality.blur_and_elevation: Window blur of 40px; three depth levels: window at 0pt, modal at 20pt to 40pt in front and tooltip at 8pt in front, with shadows of 0 20px 60px, 0 12px 40px and 0 4px 16px.

ornamentation_details.iconography: Filled and outline symbols with a 2pt stroke at 24pt to 32pt inside 44pt to 60pt circular hit areas; symbols in white with vibrancy and one tinted active state.
ornamentation_details.illustration: Real 3D objects in volumes, with soft light, real shadows and 4:3 or 1:1 bounds; flat illustration appears only in windows.

motion.transition_physics: Springs with slight damping: windows scale from 0.95 to 1.0 and fade in over 400ms; a gazed element grows a highlight in 150ms; moves toward the viewer stay under 40pt to avoid discomfort.
motion.hover_and_active: Gaze lights the target with a rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.2) fill and a 1.05 scale; pinch shows a 0.97 scale with a 0.3 alpha fill; release returns to rest over 200ms.

emotion.target_response: Calm presence: the viewer feels that the interface shares the room with them and does not take it over.

use_cases: web marketing pages for spatial devices
avoid_when: The target is a flat screen with pointer input, because 60pt targets and 40px blur waste space and GPU time there.
The environment is uncontrolled and the content needs a guaranteed contrast ratio, because the room shows through the glass.
The user session is long and dense with text, because floating glass at 2 metres tires the eyes.

modifiers.how: Make the window fill rgba(28, 28, 30, 0.85) with a blur of 12px; keep the 32pt radius and the 60pt targets.
Add a 135-degree gloss gradient, a 1px inner highlight and real material textures on volumes; keep the glass windows.
Drop the depth levels and the eye-tracking highlight, and use a 16px blur panel over a gradient; keep the capsule buttons.
Divide the window into rounded cells with a 16pt gap and a 24pt radius; keep the glass fill and the 60pt targets.

pack.why: Thin, round system glyphs in the platform manner, made for a round glass container.

ground.why: Spatial interfaces float glass panels in front of a soft, lit room.
